traceability.evidence:
Implementation and tests for Story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md are present and wired into the plugin and CLI:
- Core maintenance implementation (API & CLI): - src/maintenance/detect.ts - export function detectStaleAnnotations(codebasePath: string): string[] - Scans workspace using getAllFiles, parses @story annotations via regex, resolves paths against cwd and workspaceRoot, enforces project boundary via enforceProjectBoundary, and marks paths as stale when no in-project candidate exists. - Annotated with @story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md and @req REQ-MAINT-DETECT across the function and helper branches (processFileForStaleAnnotations, handleStoryMatch, getInProjectCandidates, anyInProjectCandidateExists).
- src/maintenance/update.ts - export function updateAnnotationReferences(codebasePath: string, oldPath: string, newPath: string): number - Validates root directory (exists & isDirectory); builds a regex `(@story\s*)${oldPath}` and performs targeted replacements, writing files only when content changes. - All logic annotated against Story 009.0 and @req REQ-MAINT-UPDATE.
- src/maintenance/batch.ts - export function batchUpdateAnnotations(codebasePath: string, mappings: { oldPath: string; newPath: string }[]): number - Loops over mappings, calling updateAnnotationReferences and summing counts (@req REQ-MAINT-BATCH). - export function verifyAnnotations(codebasePath: string): boolean - Calls detectStaleAnnotations and returns staleAnnotations.length === 0 (@req REQ-MAINT-VERIFY).
- src/maintenance/report.ts - export function generateMaintenanceReport(codebasePath: string): string - Uses detectStaleAnnotations and returns either "" or a newline-separated list of stale story paths (@req REQ-MAINT-REPORT, REQ-MAINT-SAFE).
- src/maintenance/utils.ts - export function getAllFiles(dir: string): string[] and internal traverseDirectory - Safe, recursive directory traversal used by maintenance tools. - Annotated for Story 009.0 with REQ-MAINT-UTILS-* requirements (supporting maintenance operations).
- src/maintenance/cli.ts (CLI entrypoint and bin target via package.json: "traceability-maint": "lib/src/maintenance/cli.js") - parseCliInput, createDefaultFlags, applyFlag, parseFlags, and specific handlers: - handleDetect(args): calls detectStaleAnnotations(root), supports --json, prints either “No stale @story annotations found.” or a list plus summary; exits with 0 or 1 (@req REQ-MAINT-DETECT, REQ-MAINT-REPORT, REQ-MAINT-SAFE). - handleVerify(args): uses verifyAnnotations(root), prints success or guidance message; exit code 0 on success, 1 on stale annotations (@req REQ-MAINT-VERIFY, REQ-MAINT-SAFE). - handleReport(args): uses generateMaintenanceReport(root), supports --format text|json, prints markdown-style report or JSON; always EXIT_OK (@req REQ-MAINT-REPORT, REQ-MAINT-SAFE). - handleUpdate(args): requires --from/--to, supports --dry-run and --json; in dry-run mode, prints non-destructive summary and uses generateMaintenanceReport to estimate impact; otherwise calls updateAnnotationReferences and prints a concise summary with updated count (@req REQ-MAINT-UPDATE, REQ-MAINT-SAFE). - printHelp(): detailed usage including commands, options, and help text for `traceability-maint` (@req REQ-MAINT-SAFE). - runMaintenanceCli wraps dispatch in try/catch, printing concise error diagnostics and using distinct exit codes: EXIT_OK=0, EXIT_STALE=1, EXIT_USAGE=2 (@req REQ-MAINT-SAFE, and maps REQ-MAINT-DETECT/VERIFY/REPORT/UPDATE/ BATCH to CLI behavior).
- src/maintenance/index.ts - Re-exports detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport, with a module-level doc block listing all 009.0 requirements (REQ-MAINT-*).
- src/index.ts - Imports maintenance API from "./maintenance" with a dedicated JSDoc block: - `@story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md` - `@req REQ-MAINTENANCE-API-EXPORT - Expose maintenance utilities alongside core plugin exports` - Builds and exports `const maintenance = { detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport }`. - Exports `{ rules, configs, maintenance }` and default export including maintenance; this provides programmatic integration of maintenance tools with the plugin.
- Tests directly tied to Story 009.0 (all with JSDoc @story pointing to docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md):
- tests/maintenance/cli.test.ts - Described as "Maintenance CLI (Story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS)". - Tests map explicitly to REQ-MAINT-*: - [REQ-MAINT-DETECT] detect exits 0 with "No stale @story annotations found." when workspace has no annotations. - [REQ-MAINT-VERIFY] verify exits 0 when annotations point to an existing story file. - [REQ-MAINT-REPORT] report prints human-readable summary including header and stale story name; exit code 0. - [REQ-MAINT-UPDATE] update modifies @story paths from old.path.md to new.path.md and exits 0. - [REQ-MAINT-SAFE] update requires --from and --to and exits 2 when missing (error + help output asserted). - [REQ-MAINT-SAFE] dry-run mode does not modify files but exits 0 and logs output. - [REQ-MAINT-DETECT] detect supports --json, returning JSON payload with `stale` array containing the stale path and exit code 1.
- tests/maintenance/detect.test.ts - [REQ-MAINT-DETECT] returns [] when no stale annotations (empty temp dir). - [REQ-MAINT-DETECT] detects stale references when @story points to a missing file.
- tests/maintenance/detect-isolated.test.ts - [REQ-MAINT-DETECT] returns [] when directory does not exist (graceful handling of missing root). - [REQ-MAINT-DETECT] detects stale annotations across nested directories (validating recursion and traversal). - [REQ-MAINT-DETECT] throws on permission denied for directories whose permissions are removed (explicitly tests the chosen error behavior). - [REQ-MAINT-DETECT] performs security validation: verifies that detectStaleAnnotations does NOT call fs.existsSync on unsafe/traversal or invalid-extension story paths, but does check normalized in-workspace paths (ties into REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION from file validation dependency and demonstrates safe handling of malicious @story values).
- tests/maintenance/update.test.ts - [REQ-MAINT-UPDATE] should return 0 when no updates made in an empty temp dir, confirming safe no-op behavior.
- tests/maintenance/update-isolated.test.ts - [REQ-MAINT-UPDATE] updates @story annotations in files (verifies that exactly one annotation is updated and content now contains new.path.md). - [REQ-MAINT-UPDATE] returns 0 when directory does not exist, confirming early exit safety.
- tests/maintenance/batch.test.ts - [REQ-MAINT-BATCH] batchUpdateAnnotations returns 0 when no mappings are supplied. - [REQ-MAINT-VERIFY] verifyAnnotations returns true when a temp workspace contains a valid @story pointing to an existing story file.
- tests/maintenance/report.test.ts - [REQ-MAINT-REPORT] generateMaintenanceReport returns empty string when no stale annotations found. - [REQ-MAINT-REPORT] generateMaintenanceReport reports stale story annotation when @story points to non-existent.story.md.
- tests/maintenance/index.test.ts - [REQ-MAINT-SAFE] Asserts that all maintenance functions are correctly exported from the maintenance module (detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport), mapping exports to REQ-MAINT-DETECT/UPDATE/BATCH/VERIFY/REPORT.
- Shared support and integration with existing validation and error infrastructure: - src/utils/storyReferenceUtils.ts (from dependency story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION) provides enforceProjectBoundary and security-oriented existence checks; detect.ts relies on enforceProjectBoundary and isUnsafeStoryPath imports, aligning maintenance tools with existing file-validation logic. - Maintenance operations use getAllFiles to handle traversal and rely on Story 006.0 utilities for boundary and security checks, satisfying dependencies 005.0/006.0/007.0 about understanding formats, file existence, and consistent error handling.
- CLI and API documentation (fulfilling Documentation acceptance criterion): - README.md – "Maintenance CLI" section - Explains the `traceability-maint` CLI, lists commands (detect, verify, report, update) and describes what each does. - Provides concrete usage examples: - `npx traceability-maint --help` - `npx traceability-maint detect --root .` - `npx traceability-maint verify --root .` - `npx traceability-maint report --root . --format json` - `npx traceability-maint update --root . --from ... --to ...`
- user-docs/api-reference.md – "Maintenance API and CLI" section - Documents programmatic API: - detectStaleAnnotations(rootDir) - updateAnnotationReferences(rootDir, oldPath, newPath) - batchUpdateAnnotations(rootDir, mappings) - verifyAnnotations(rootDir) - generateMaintenanceReport(rootDir) - Details parameters, return values, and behavior notes that align with actual implementations (e.g., early return 0 / [] when root does not exist; only touching @story annotations; no side effects for report). - Documents `traceability-maint` CLI commands, options, and exit codes (0 success, 1 stale/invalid annotations, 2 usage/config error) that match src/maintenance/cli.ts behavior.
- Integration into project structure and tooling: - package.json - "bin": { "traceability-maint": "lib/src/maintenance/cli.js" } – ensures the maintenance CLI is available when the package is built and installed. - Scripts include `ci-verify` and related commands that would exercise type-check, lint, and tests including the maintenance tests. - jest.config.js - testMatch: ["/tests/**/*.test.ts"] – includes tests/maintenance/*.test.ts so Story 009.0 tests are part of the main test suite. - src/index.ts - Exposes `maintenance` object alongside plugin rules and configs, allowing consumers to access maintenance tools through the primary package export, satisfying the integration aspect of the story.
- Test execution: - The configured test command in package.json is `"test": "jest --ci --bail"`. - Running `npm test -- --runInBand --verbose` executes Jest with the configured suite; the tool output shows Jest is invoked without reporting failures (`> jest --ci --bail --runInBand --verbose` and no error trace), indicating the test suite including maintenance tests passes under this configuration.
Taken together, the code, tests, CLI wiring, exports, and documentation directly implement REQ-MAINT-DETECT, REQ-MAINT-UPDATE, REQ-MAINT-BATCH, REQ-MAINT-VERIFY, REQ-MAINT-REPORT, and REQ-MAINT-SAFE for Story 009.0 and satisfy the acceptance criteria for core functionality, integration, user feedback, error handling for missing and invalid paths, and documentation.
traceability.notes: Story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS is fully implemented. There is a dedicated maintenance module (detect, update, batch, verify, report, traversal utils), a `traceability-maint` CLI with subcommands and clear exit codes, and programmatic exports through the main plugin index. Each requirement (REQ-MAINT-DETECT/UPDATE/BATCH/VERIFY/REPORT/SAFE) is covered by both implementation and targeted Jest tests under tests/maintenance, all of which reference this story via @story annotations. The README and user-docs/api-reference.md document the maintenance API and CLI with concrete usage examples. Tests are integrated into the main Jest suite and run via `npm test`. The implementation matches the acceptance criteria: it detects stale references, supports batch and single-path updates, preserves code behavior by only modifying @story values, integrates with existing file-validation utilities, returns appropriate exit codes with human-readable and JSON output, and is thoroughly documented.
